applies_to: Carrier AquaSnap 30RC 065-252 air-cooled scroll chillers (including Greenspeed intelligence models) with the Carrier Controller.
summary: The 30RC 065-252's Carrier Controller serves BACnet IP on its Ethernet port and BACnet MS/TP on an RS-485 port, enabled from the BACnet Standard Conf. menu. The object table has about 740 objects: command points come as read (_rd) and write (_wr) pairs with the writable copies at 10000+ instances, plus temperatures, pressures, circuit, fan and pump drive data, and one BV per Carrier alarm code (e.g. BV 101199).
notes: This is the larger 30RC 065-252 range; the 30RC 010-060 has its own, much shorter list (30RC-101T).
Points are from the "BACnet 2" object table. The "BACnet 1" table before it is a trend log list (object name, log interval, trend log instance) with no object types, so it is not reproduced.
Access is from the PV ACCESS column: RW and WO as writable, RO as read-only. BV 5320 DCFC_STA_m_dcfc is printed NA and is listed as read-only.
No units column; temperatures follow the BACnet Metric Unit setting (bacunit, default Yes).
Free cooling, heat reclaim, heat pump, electric heat and pump drive points only apply to units with those options.

source.title: AquaSnap 30RC 065-252 Air-Cooled Chillers with Carrier Controller - Controls, Start-Up, Operation, Service and Troubleshooting (Appendix D, BACnet IP and MS/TP Points)

integration.summary: Enable BACnet (bacena) under Main Menu > Configuration > Network > BACnet, set the device ID and network, then select the Network control method with the Start/Stop button. Command through the _wr objects (start/stop, occupancy, control point, demand limit) and read run status, water temperatures, capacity and alarms.

integration.enable: Select the Network machine control method with the Start/Stop button; the unit then follows CCN, BACnet (if enabled) or Modbus (if enabled) commands and ignores the remote control contacts. Start/stop and occupancy are written to the _wr objects.
integration.heartbeat: The manual says that if communication with the network is lost, the machine starts and is controlled locally.
setup: BACnet Enable (bacena) defaults to Disable; the appendix lists 1 = BACnet IP and 2 = BACnet MS/TP.
Defaults shown: network 1600, UDP port 47808, manual device ID 1600001, auto device ID option off, alarm reporting on.
IP port interface option 0 = J5/J15, 1 = J16.
gotchas: Write the _wr object, not the _rd one; the _rd copy only reports the current value.

The BACnet menu has a BACnet Manage Occupancy option (mng_occ, default No) and the list has a writable BACnet_BMS_OCC (AV 66, 0 = unocc, 1 = occ, 2 = none); check how they interact with CHIL_OCC before relying on either.
